title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an artificial intelligence scribe record her first urologist appointment, but the tool invented a claim that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms. The false statement appeared in a post-operative letter sent to her GP after kidney stone surgery, causing her distress because she feared it could affect her workers' compensation case. After she complained, the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

A report by Digital Rights Watch found AI medical scribes can hallucinate serious errors, such as recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis, and that consent practices vary widely. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates about 40 per cent of GPs regularly use these tools. Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration has been reviewing AI scribes and says its findings will be released in the coming weeks, with any breaches acted upon.
